name: Viewport meta and visual viewport
plain: visualViewport reports pinch-zoom scale and on-screen keyboard offsets.
meaning: Scale above 1 tells the person is zoomed in (accessibility); height shrink exposes the on-screen keyboard. Updates live as the user pinches or types.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can see your pinch zoom level and when the on screen keyboard pops up
limits.user_action: You pinch to zoom, or tap a box that opens the keyboard.
can: Check your current pinch zoom scale
See changes to the visible area, such as when the keyboard opens
Move buttons so they stay above the keyboard
cannot: See what you type on the keyboard
Tell which keyboard app you use

story.what_it_is: Reports pinch zoom level and how far the on screen keyboard has pushed the page.

marketing.name: Visual Viewport API
marketing.pitch: Explains how a page can read the part of the page currently visible, including zoom and keyboard changes.

story.for_you: You never see the reading. It is why a chat box slides up neatly above the keyboard when you start typing on your phone.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to keep inputs visible and to adapt to zoom. The same numbers can show how a person holds and uses a device, which fraud teams can use.

use_cases.example: A chat site lifts the message box above the on screen keyboard so you can see what you type.
A browser game keeps its controls on screen when the keyboard opens for chat.
A web map redraws labels when you pinch to zoom.
A checkout form scrolls the card number field into view when the keyboard pops up.
A bot check sees a browser that never pinch zooms or shows a keyboard on a supposed phone.
A site keeps text readable when a user zooms in a lot.
A drawing app tells drawing taps apart from zoom gestures.

technical_bounds: Browser pinch scale differs per OS
